[0] everyday_reading (E): Everyday reading: quotation marks are just decoration, and spacing inside them is tidied up like ordinary text; single and double quotes mean the same thing. Java rule: characters within double quotes are taken literally (every space counts), the quotes are not part of the value, and single quotes are for one char.

[0] names_the_element (N): A string literal is a sequence of characters written in double quotes in the source code, e.g. "Hello, World"; it is a value of type String.
[1] states_the_rule (S): A String literal is enclosed in a pair of double quotes; everything inside is taken literally, special characters such as " and newline are written with escape sequences, and the literal must close on the same source line.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): The literal is a constant: it is fixed at compile time and simply supplies its value when the expression containing it is evaluated.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Value is the String of the characters between the quotes (escape sequences replaced by the characters they stand for), without the quotes: "Hi, " has 4 characters, and printing it shows Hi, followed by a space.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): Evaluating a literal changes no state; it just yields the same String value every time.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): print("s") outputs exactly the characters between the quotes, without the quotes.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): println("s") outputs exactly the characters between the quotes and then ends the line.
[2] relation_to_neighbour (R): Escape sequences (\n, \t, \", \\) are written inside string or char literals to stand for one character that cannot be typed directly.
[3] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Purpose: state fixed text exactly, such as messages, labels and prompts, so you can precisely specify what gets printed.

[0] predict_a_change (C): Changing any character inside the quotes (including adding a space) changes the output by exactly that character; changing spaces outside the quotes changes nothing.
[1] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: A String literal is enclosed in a pair of double quotes. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: a missing closing (or opening) quote; the compiler may get very confused and report errors elsewhere
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: String literals use double quotes; single quotes are for one char. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: 'Hello' (more than one character in single quotes): unclosed character literal
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: A string literal must not span source lines. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: a line break inside "...": unclosed string literal
[4] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use a string literal for fixed text known when the program is written; use args, input or variables for text that varies between runs, and char literals for a single character.
[5] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: A double quote inside a string must be escaped. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: "She said "Hi"" without \"
